title: HCP — Query Context — payload
description: The request payload of the HCP 2.0-draft-3 Query operation (HCP 5.2.1): a Context Client asks a provider for the context relevant to a query, for a named purpose, under the grant its access token stands for. The outer document members (id, type, issuer, recipient, issuedAt, expiresAt, proof) are owned by the framework — SPEC §6.3.

query.description: HCP `query`: what the client wants context about, in natural language. HCP treats query text as being as sensitive as content (HCP 8.2), so the provider does not log it.

categories.description: HCP `categories`: the categories to search. Absent means every category the grant covers. A category outside the grant is refused with `permissionDenied` (HCP 5.2.1). The bound of 256 is a framework bound, not an HCP requirement.

purpose.description: HCP `purpose`: the purpose code, an absolute URI, the context is requested for. It must be a purpose the grant allows (HCP 5.2.1).

purposeDescription.description: HCP `purposeDescription`: a human-readable statement of the purpose. Absent when the client gives none.

maxEntries.description: HCP `maxEntries`: the most entries the client wants. Absent means HCP's default of 5. The provider returns at most the lesser of this value and 20 (HCP 7.2).

accessToken.description: The HCP access token (an OAuth or first-party token, HCP 9.3) that stands for the grant, carried unchanged. HCP's HTTP binding sends it as a Bearer token; this member carries it in the document. The provider validates it exactly as over HTTP and treats it as opaque.

Response.title: HCP — Query Context — response payload
Response.description: The HCP Query result: the disclosed entries, ordered by the provider's declared method, with the directives that apply to them. Failures use trust-task-error, not this shape.

entries.description: HCP `entries`: at most 20 entries (HCP 7.2), each a Disclosure, or an Entry where HCP lets the reader see the entry itself. Empty when nothing matched or nothing could be disclosed.

retrievalId.description: HCP `retrievalId`: the identifier of this retrieval, as recorded in the provider's `context.read` audit event (HCP 8.1).

minimization.description: HCP `minimization`: the provider's account of how it minimized the result (HCP 7.2), carried as HCP defines it.

categoriesSearched.description: HCP `categoriesSearched`: the categories the provider searched.

directives.description: HCP `directives`: the directives that apply to the disclosed context (HCP 6.4). Absent when none applies.

respondedAt.description: HCP `timestamp`, renamed: when the provider produced the result.
